scope_of_this_run: F05 (R04 dependency/lifecycle) -- partial. Two concrete, code-audited-and-verified defects fixed: (1) /v1/graph/explore anchor resolved_id vs exclude_source_types inconsistency when the representative copy is excluded, (2) ingest pipeline's content-hash-unchanged skip branch never restoring Document.status from archived to active (asymmetric with the adjacent hash-changed branch, which always restores). A third suspected defect (lexicon_version bumping on no-op seed re-runs) was investigated and empirically disproven -- a regression-guard test was added instead of a fix.
deliberately_not_started_this_run: Dependency-revision + invalidation-queue mechanism for lexicon-revision / late-ingested-reference-target / representative-swap recompute triggers (handoff 2.5.1/2.5.2/2.5.7). Requires a new table + migration; per handoff section 3.4, any change needing a backfill must go to the user as a separate approval item with impact diff, backfill scope, abort criteria, and recovery plan. Not attempted without that gate.

Namespace partitioning of build_page_identity_index by identity domain (page vs ticket) instead of source_type (handoff 2.5.3/2.5.6). Code-audit-confirmed as still a gap (identity separation today is incidental, via a hardcoded source_type allowlist reimplemented in 3 places), but changing index partitioning changes which references resolve at all -- existing prod edges would go stale until a resync, which also needs the same separate-approval gate.
Default exposure policy for inactive/archived documents (opt-in audit flag) -- handoff 2.5.5. No code written this run.

Read-only classification query for production's 201 unresolved_references, to be run by the user against prod (dev has not been resynced since this feature existed, so a dev-side sample would not represent production -- user-confirmed constraint from earlier in this session).

investigated_and_found_not_to_be_a_bug.claim: seed_lexicon()'s apply loop unconditionally reassigns row.variants/priority/metadata_ even when nothing changed (plan.action==noop), suspected to bump lexicon_terms.updated_at via onupdate=func.now() on every no-op seed re-run, which would break using lexicon_version as a stable per-doc invalidation signal.
investigated_and_found_not_to_be_a_bug.finding: Empirically false. SQLAlchemy's scalar attribute change-tracking does not mark the row dirty when the reassigned value equals the already-loaded value (confirmed for both plain scalars and a freshly-constructed-but-content-equal JSONB dict), so no UPDATE is issued and updated_at does not move. A regression-guard test (test_seed_lexicon_noop_does_not_bump_updated_at) was added to protect this going forward, since F05's planned lexicon-revision invalidation signal depends on it staying stable.

document_status_writer_audit.method: Full-codebase grep + manual review via a dedicated exploration pass (not just the explore survey) -- see commit a57beda's description.
document_status_writer_audit.finding: No manual, per-document, API-driven archive/unarchive endpoint exists anywhere in apps/api. Every Document.status write is either (a) fully automatic crawl-detected page removal (app/confluence/map_sync.py), (b) a CLI-only, space-level bulk archive with no HTTP route (app/confluence/map_space_setup.py --apply), or (c) the ingest pipeline setting/resetting status on insert/update. The 'superseded' and 'draft_insight' status values are documented in the model comment but never written or read anywhere in the app.
